title: When They Say: «I Don't Want to Pray»
summary:
A day will come when your child says: «I don't want to pray.» They may say it while busy playing, or tired, or because prayer feels long and boring, or because they want to see what you will do. This moment is a test for you before it is a test for them.

The first thing to do: stay calm. Shouting and threats may make them pray today, but they tie prayer in their heart to fear and pressure. Rifq (gentleness) in this situation is not weakness. The Prophet ﷺ said: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ فِي الأَمْرِ كُلِّهِ» (Sahih al-Bukhari 6927)

Then look for the reason with a calm question: «What makes you not want to pray now?» If they are absorbed in play, give a short, clear grace period: «Play for five more minutes, then we'll pray together.» If they are tired, offer to pray together right now so they can rest after. If they are bored, ask them how you could make prayer nicer: a spot they choose, or letting them be the one who calls the iqamah.

Avoid a long battle of wills: state your request once, clearly, then wait calmly, and repeat it a little later without getting worked up. Each prayer's time extends beyond the adhan, so offer them two suitable choices within the time, such as: «Shall we pray now or in five minutes?», leaving enough time for wudu and prayer; feeling they have a choice softens stubbornness. When they pray after an initial refusal, praise them without blaming them for what came before. And if the refusal repeats every day along with stubbornness about many things, look at the wider picture: do they get more of your attention when they refuse than when they cooperate?
try_this: Today: Write a calm sentence to say to your child if they refuse to pray, offering a clear grace period, such as: «Play for five more minutes, then we'll pray Asr together.» Say it once quietly to yourself so it is ready when you need it.
reflection_prompts: What is the most common reason behind your child's refusal to pray — tiredness, play or boredom — and how did you find out?
